problem: "Availability ... is a dependability attribute (reliability in service)" blurs two separate ideas that the chapter's own table lists side by side under dependability. Availability is the fraction of time the system is up; reliability is the chance it runs without failing for a stated period. A student can read the bracket and use the words as synonyms in an answer.
fix: (a) Being up for 99.9 % of the year is availability, a dependability attribute. Reliability (failure-free running for a stated period) is a different measure.

problem: It says architectural design is picked out because "the next chapter builds on it", but Section 3 points architectural styles to 3.3 while the next chapter (3.2) is the modular/object-oriented design material. The caption and the cross-references disagree.
fix: Architectural design is picked out because the architectural styles and patterns chapters (3.3 and 3.4) build on it.

problem: "Every design decision buys one attribute and costs another" is put as a law. Some decisions are neutral or improve two attributes at once; the useful rule is that a reviewer must look for the trade-off, not assume exactly one of each.
fix: Most design decisions buy one attribute at the cost of another, and a good design review names both sides.
